claims.text: A standard sintered W–Cu composite consists of tungsten particles embedded in a continuous copper matrix.
Pre-coating tungsten particles with nanoscale Mo before consolidation will produce a thin, continuous Mo interlayer at the W/Cu interface.
A Mo interlayer will improve thermal coupling between tungsten and copper.
The Mo interlayer will reduce W/Cu interfacial thermal resistance.
Mo acts as a phonon bridge that reduces vibrational mismatch at the W/Cu interface.
Reduced vibrational mismatch decreases thermal boundary resistance.
Mo is chemically and mechanically compatible with both tungsten and copper.
The compatibility of the Mo interlayer with both phases will preserve the composite's mechanical integrity.
The Mo interlayer will preserve irradiation resistance.
The Mo-coated W–Cu composite will have significantly higher thermal conductivity than an otherwise identical uncoated W–Cu composite.
The Mo-coated composite will retain mechanical strength comparable to the uncoated control.
The Mo-coated composite will retain resistance to irradiation-induced degradation comparable to the uncoated control.
Fusion-reactor applications impose elevated-temperature and irradiation-resistance requirements on candidate materials.
The proposed benefit should persist during high-temperature thermal cycling and irradiation representative of fusion-reactor joints.
The magnitude of thermal-conductivity improvement depends on Mo-coating uniformity, coating thickness, and processing parameters.
